batch.title: Agroforestry QA (22 Oct 2026): high-leverage units + random sample
batch.notes: Risk-based QA of the agroforestry effect evidence. 166 high-leverage units (each alone flips a class or deletes a row — the leave-one-out list), 2 flagged cards, and a random 40 (20 general + 20 newly voting cocoa/coffee F5 units) so an error rate can be stated for the unreviewed rest. Approve = encoding faithful; reject = wrong (pick a reason); hold = you want my assessment.

units.citation: Montagnini, F.; Somarriba, E.; Murgueitio, E.; Fassola, H.; Eibl, B. (eds.) (2015). Sistemas agroforestales. Funciones productivas, socioeconómicas y ambientales. CATIE (Turrialba) / CIPAV (Cali). [series number to confirm from PDF]
units.quote: Para el caso de la Reserva Natural El Hatico, el cambio hacia SSPi permitió eliminar el riego en los potreros sin efectos notables sobre la producción. Esto se logró incluso durante al menos dos eventos de El Niño, caracterizados por una fuerte reducción de la precipitación en Colombia, incluyendo el año 2009, en el que se registró la menor precipitación en varias décadas (440 mm anuales), a pesar de lo cual se logró un aumento del 10% en la producción de leche con respecto al año anterior (Murgueitio et al. 2011). (English: At El Hatico Nature Reserve, the switch to intensive silvopastoral systems made it possible to eliminate pasture irrigation with no notable effect on production. This was achieved even during at least two El Niño events, characterised by a strong reduction of rainfall in Colombia, including 2009, which recorded the lowest rainfall in several decades (440 mm per year), despite which milk production increased by 10% relative to the previous year (Murgueitio et al. 2011).)

relationship.outcome_raw: milk production in the El Nino year with la menor precipitación en varias décadas rose relative to the previous year after conversion to intensive silvopasture, without irrigation

context.severity_cue: la menor precipitación en varias décadas
context.note: single farm; year-on-year comparison, not a with/without contrast

units.citation: Santos et al. (2025). Sistemas Agroflorestais no Semiárido Brasileiro: Uma Revisão sobre Viabilidade, Benefícios Econômicos e Ecológicos. Revista Brasileira de Geografia Física.
units.quote: Avaliando as áreas que apresentaram níveis críticos para os animais, os autores obtiveram reduções variando de 20 até 100% ao comparar os sistemas agroflorestais com a monocultura. Demostrando a importância desses sistemas no conforto animal, reduzindo o estresse por calor, como uma importante estratégia para às crescentes temperatura advindas das mudanças climáticas. (English: Assessing the areas that presented critical levels for the animals, the authors obtained reductions varying from 20 to 100% when comparing the agroforestry systems with the monoculture. Demonstrating the importance of these systems for animal comfort, reducing heat stress, as an important strategy for the rising temperatures arising from climate change.)

units.citation: Quandt, A. et al. (2017). The role of agroforestry in building livelihood resilience to floods and drought in semiarid Kenya. Ecology and Society.
units.quote: Some of the ecological characteristics of agroforestry species make them resilient to floods and droughts, including deep root systems that are able to use a greater soil volume for water and nutrients (Kandji et al. 2006, Verchot et al. 2007). Shade trees can produce microclimates that buffer temperature fluctuations (Lin 2007), which in turn can reduce evapotranspiration. Further, trees have the ability to buffer crops from storms (Philpott et al. 2008).

relationship.outcome_raw: buffer from storms

units.citation: Reed et al. (2017). Trees for life: The ecosystem service contribution of trees to food production and livelihoods in the tropics. Forest Policy and Economics.
units.quote: The main difference when comparing the effects of trees on yields with the overall livelihood effects of trees across all studies is the reduc- tion in the total negative effects from 36% for yield to 16% for overall livelihood effects, suggesting that a reduction in yields may be compen- sated by other beneﬁts provided by trees to the farm system (Fig. 6). This cost/beneﬁt relationship—where the cost of crop yield losses is compensated by the overall beneﬁts of incorporating trees—is consis- tent across the study regions with Africa, Asia and the Americas reporting negative effects of trees on crop yields in 33%, 48%, and 33% of studies but negative effects of trees on overall livelihood outcomes in only 15%, 24%, and 8% respectively (Fig. 7).

relationship.outcome_raw: negative effects of trees on crop yields reported in 33% (Africa), 48% (Asia) and 33% (Americas) of studies, but negative effects on OVERALL LIVELIHOOD outcomes in only 15%, 24% and 8% respectively

context.note: THE UNSUITABLE TAIL: a third to a half of studies record yield LOSSES from tree presence. Asia carries the largest yield penalty. VOTE-COUNT review: percentages are shares of STUDIES reporting a direction, not effect magnitudes, so metric = narrative. PICOS: 58 of the 74 reviewed studies are agroforestry studies and 53 of those are trees INTRODUCED TO THE FARM (typically alley cropping); only 12 studies concern off-farm natural forest patches. The pooled vote-counts are therefore dominated by, but not exclusive to, agroforestry — read as agroforestry-weighted, not agroforestry-pure.

units.quote: Sgarbossa et al. (2018) avaliando a influência de diferentes sistemas agroflorestais e da poda de árvores sobre a radiação solar na produtividade da soja, obtiveram maior rendimento na monocultura com valores em torno de 3000 (2013/2014) e 2700 kg ha-1 (2014/2015), enquanto os sistemas agroflorestais apresentaram valores em torno de 500 (2013/2014) e 700 kg ha-1 (2014/2015). Os autores atribuíram tal discrepância principalmente pela maior incidência de radiação no monocultivo, denotando a importância do manejo para melhor interação entre os componentes do sistema. (English: Sgarbossa et al. (2018), assessing the influence of different agroforestry systems and tree pruning on solar radiation in soybean productivity, obtained higher yield in monoculture with values around 3000 (2013/2014) and 2700 kg ha-1 (2014/2015), while the agroforestry systems showed values around 500 (2013/2014) and 700 kg ha-1 (2014/2015). The authors attributed this discrepancy mainly to the greater incidence of radiation in the monoculture, highlighting the importance of management for better interaction between the components of the system.)

relationship.outcome_raw: soybean yield about 500 and 700 kg/ha in agroforestry versus about 3000 and 2700 kg/ha in monoculture over two seasons

context.note: large negative finding retained; authors attribute it to lower radiation in the agroforestry treatment

units.citation: Navas Panadero (2010). Importancia de los sistemas silvopastoriles en la reducción del estrés calórico en sistemas de producción ganadera tropical. Revista de Medicina Veterinaria.
units.quote: Los periodos de sequía en el trópico se caracterizan por altas temperaturas y forrajes de baja calidad que son poco aprovechados por los animales, los cua- les en algunos casos pierden peso en estas épocas. Restrepo (2001) encontró en la época seca mayores ganancias de peso (2 a 5%) en animales que pasto- reaban potreros con alta densidad de árboles, que aquellos que estaban en zonas de baja cobertura, esto se puede atribuir, en parte, a mayores tiempos de pastoreo y rumia producto de la reducción del es- trés calórico. (English: Drought periods in the tropics are characterised by high temperatures and low-quality forage that animals use poorly, and in some cases they lose weight in these periods. Restrepo (2001) found higher weight gains (2 to 5%) in the dry season in animals grazing pastures with high tree density than in those in low-cover areas, which can be attributed in part to longer grazing and rumination times resulting from reduced heat stress.)

units.citation: Souza et al. (2011). Resistência de espécies arbóreas submetidas a extremos climáticos de geada em diferentes sistemas agroflorestais. Ciência Rural.
units.quote: Na linha de plantio do SL, observou-se um dossel fechado, formado pela copa das plantas, fato que pode estar diretamente ligado à mudança de condições microclimáticas, beneficiando de maneira positiva a espécie. Espera-se que o dossel tenha proporcionado menores perdas noturnas de radiação, como demonstrado nos trabalhos conduzidos por MARIN et al. (2003) e PILAU et al. (2007), interferindo nos valores de temperatura mínima, ou seja, interferindo no resfriamento noturno, resultando no maior acúmulo de calor e menor dano na planta. (English: In the planting row of the line system a closed canopy formed by the plant crowns was observed, a fact that may be directly linked to a change in microclimatic conditions, benefiting the species positively. The canopy is expected to have produced lower night-time radiation losses, as shown in the work by MARIN et al. (2003) and PILAU et al. (2007), affecting minimum temperature values, that is, affecting night-time cooling, resulting in greater heat accumulation and less damage to the plant.)

relationship.outcome_raw: closed canopy in the denser line arrangement reduced night-time radiative loss, raising minimum temperature and lowering frost damage

context.note: counter-example to cold-air-pooling: canopy closure REDUCED frost damage here

units.citation: Baker et al. (2025). Effect of silvopasture, paddock trees and linear agroforestry systems on agricultural productivity: A global quantitative analysis. Agricultural Systems.
units.quote:
The paddock- 
level yield dataset included 32 studies with 255 paddock years. Three 
studies included in the distance-based response dataset were excluded 
from the paddock-level dataset as they were based on modelled data 
from a combination of paddocks.
On average, the paddock-level dataset showed a negative effect size, 
with windbreak paddocks having a reduced yield of 8.3 % compared to 
paddocks with no windbreaks, excluding the area of land occupied by 
the trees. However, the standard deviation across studies was quite large 
(± 36.8 %). More responses showed a decreased yield (n = 171) than an 
increased yield (n = 83), while one paddock showed no change.

units.citation: Reed et al. (2017). Trees for life: The ecosystem service contribution of trees to food production and livelihoods in the tropics. Forest Policy and Economics.
units.quote: The overall trend across the studies shows that in the majority of cases (52%) there was a net positive (47%) or neutral (5%) effect of tree presence on food yields or food yield proxies. However, when the results are disaggregated by region, there is a degree of variability (Fig. 5). For example, in the Americas and Asia, tree presence was more likely to enhance food yields with positive effects of trees on yields reported in 58% and 54% of studies for these regions respectively; while in Asia the opposite is the case, with the majority of studies (48%) reporting decreased food yields as a result of tree presence (Fig. 5).

relationship.outcome_raw: in the majority of cases (52%) tree presence had a net positive (47%) or neutral (5%) effect on food yields or yield proxies; regionally, positive effects were reported in 58% (Americas) and 54% (Asia) of studies while a further statement reports 48% of studies in one region recording DECREASED yields

context.note: HEADLINE. QUEUE/SOURCE CAVEAT: the regional sentence names 'Asia' twice with opposite signs — an apparent typo in the published text (the 48%-decrease region is almost certainly Africa per the later regional breakdown 33%/48%/33%). Not resolvable from the text, so no regional unit emitted from this sentence. VOTE-COUNT review: percentages are shares of STUDIES reporting a direction, not effect magnitudes, so metric = narrative. PICOS: 58 of the 74 reviewed studies are agroforestry studies and 53 of those are trees INTRODUCED TO THE FARM (typically alley cropping); only 12 studies concern off-farm natural forest patches. The pooled vote-counts are therefore dominated by, but not exclusive to, agroforestry — read as agroforestry-weighted, not agroforestry-pure.

units.quote: Asimismo, en Colombia fue posible incrementar el nivel de carga animal a 4.3 vacas ha-1 y la produc- ción de leche al 130 %, además de eliminar comple- tamente el uso de fertilizantes químicos, al emplear un SSP compuesto de pastos, árboles de tamaño grande y medio y arbustos de Leucaena. También en las épocas de sequía intensa se mantuvo cons- tante la producción de forraje y se pudo neutralizar los efectos negativos en todo el sistema silvopasto- ril, al compararse con el monocultivo de gramíneas, en el que se redujo la biomasa al 25 % (Altieri y Nicholls, 2013). (English: Likewise, in Colombia it was possible to raise stocking to 4.3 cows ha-1 and milk production to 130%, while completely eliminating chemical fertilisers, using a silvopastoral system of pastures, large and medium trees and Leucaena shrubs. Also, in periods of intense drought forage production stayed constant and the negative effects on the whole silvopastoral system could be neutralised, compared with grass monoculture, in which biomass was reduced to 25% (Altieri and Nicholls, 2013).)

units.citation: Baker et al. (2025). Effect of silvopasture, paddock trees and linear agroforestry systems on agricultural productivity: A global quantitative analysis. Agricultural Systems.
units.quote:
Only a limited number of studies were identified (12 publications 
containing 36 paddock years) that reported the impact of linear agro­
forestry on effect size of animal yield. Yield data encompassed a range of 
types including livestock weight, carrying capacity and wool yield. Data 
on livestock mortality and health were excluded from the analyses due 
to insufficient replication. A two-sided t-test was used to determine if the 
studies deviated from the control value of 100 % yield. There was no 
significant difference in yield response from the control value (t =
−1.07, P = 0.290); the average effect size across all paddock years was a 
0.3 % reduction, with 50–50 split of responses reporting positive or 
negative effect sizes.

relationship.outcome_raw: livestock yield (weight, carrying capacity, wool) in linear agroforestry (alleys + windbreaks) vs control: 0.3 % reduction, not significant, a 50–50 split of positive and negative responses

context.note: global quantitative review (Web of Science to April 2021) of productivity in agroforestry vs a treeless control or the furthest reported distance; effect size = % change vs control per paddock-year; country mix not given in the main text (income group left blank, not guessed). Family cross_family because the livestock analysis pools alley (planted_silvoarable) and windbreak (linear_boundary) systems.

units.citation: (2024). Bilan et analyse des interventions et expérimentations agroforestières au regard de leur potentiel à contribuer à l'adaption aux changements climatiques au Sénégal. .
units.quote: La littérature scientifique ne rapporte en outre pas de consensus clair quant aux effets que les haies brise-vent engendrent en période de sécheresse. Certaines études pointent le fait que le rendement de plusieurs cultures établies à proximité de haies brise-vent serait accru durant les années plus sèches (Kanzler et al., 2018; Nuberg, 1998; Thevathasan et Gordon, 2004), tandis que d’autres jugent que l’effet des haies pourrait alors nuire aux cultures non irriguées (FAO, 1986). (English: The scientific literature moreover reports no clear consensus as to the effects that windbreak hedges produce during periods of drought. Some studies point out that the yield of several crops established near windbreak hedges would be increased during drier years (Kanzler et al., 2018; Nuberg, 1998; Thevathasan and Gordon, 2004), while others judge that the effect of the hedges could then harm non-irrigated crops (FAO, 1986).)

relationship.outcome_raw: no clear consensus on windbreak effects during drought: some studies find higher yields in drier years, others find harm to rainfed crops

context.note: explicit disagreement statement - feeds the IPCC agreement axis

units.quote: En effet, la présence d’arbres associés à une culture tamponne la température de l’air et du sol, diminue la vitesse des vents, ainsi que la quantité et la qualité de lumière transmise. Enfin, elle augmente l’humidité relative de l’air et l’humidité des sols sous canopée (Avelino et al., 2011). (English: Indeed, the presence of trees associated with a crop buffers air and soil temperature, reduces wind speed, and reduces the quantity and quality of transmitted light. Finally, it increases the relative humidity of the air and the soil moisture under the canopy (Avelino et al., 2011).)

units.citation: Sida et al. (2018). Climate-smart agroforestry:  Faidherbia albida  trees buffer wheat against climatic extremes in the Central Rift Valley of Ethiopia. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology.
units.quote:
Air temperature was lowered by up to 6°C at midday under compared to outside the canopy 
of F. albida (Figure 4.3c). Temperature reached 36oC and was highly variable in the open field, 
while it reached a maximum of 29oC and fluctuated less under the canopy. Temperature 
exceeded 28oC, for about six hours day-1 (i.e., from 10:00-16:00 GMT) in the open fields and 
for less than two hours (i.e., from 12:300-14:300 GMT) for under the canopy. For close to three 
hours around midday (i.e. from 10:40-13:30 GMT), temperature was significantly cooler under 
tree crowns than in open fields (P<0.001).

relationship.outcome_raw: midday air temperature at wheat floral height under F. albida canopy vs open field, anthesis to grain filling

context.practice_as_described: wheat grown under the crowns of scattered mature on-farm Faidherbia albida parkland trees (5.6 trees/ha, heavily pruned by farmers) vs sole wheat in the open field at least 70 m from any tree; both fertilised identically (64 kg N + 30 kg P per ha), weed-free, farmers' typical practice
context.note: on-farm paired-plot experiment, 3 farms x 3 seasons (2013-2015); chapter 4 of Sida WUR thesis, journal version Agric. For. Meteorol. 2018; tree is Faidherbia albida (the parkland's dominant species in the study area), host crop wheat - tagged practice_technology as a parkland-on-cropland effect, orchestrator may retag; heat stress named by the authors on p94 ('F. albida buffered wheat against heat stress at critical reproductive stages'); open-field peak 36 C vs 29 C under canopy (same page)

units.quote: Studies on water regulation were conducted in 12 countries. In total, 96 observations were identified from 38 studies that ful- filled the selection criteria. units.citation: Muchane et al. (2020). Agroforestry boosts soil health in the humid and sub-humid tropics: A meta-analysis. Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment.
units.quote: Data on available N were found in 34 studies with a total of 117 RR values. Figure 6a gives the 300 estimated values of effect sizes for each study and the overall mean. The overall mean RR (1.46; CL: 301 1.32-1.59) was significantly greater than 1 indicating that soil available N under agroforestry was 46% 302 higher than in crop monocultures (Figure 6a). The increase in soil N availability was most readily 303 detected as nitrate-N rather than as ammonium-N. Soil N availability did not significantly vary with 304 agroforestry management, ability to fix N or soil texture (Figure 6b). However, agroforestry increased 305 available soil N by up to 52% on clay soils as compared to the 25% increase on loamy soils (Figure 6b).

relationship.outcome_raw: system water use efficiency (above-ground biomass per unit seasonal water use, g/kg), gliricidia + maize + pigeonpea vs maize + pigeonpea, one season (Table 1)

context.practice_as_described: Gliricidia sepium trees planted in alternate furrows between maize ridges (0.5 m within, 1.5 m between rows), pruned to 30 cm above ground 2-4 weeks before crop planting and again when maize reached ca. 60 cm (and whenever shading maize); prunings incorporated into the ridges / top-dressed as green leaf manure (GLM); no inorganic fertiliser; trees left unpruned after maize harvest; GMP arm additionally intercrops pigeonpea on the ridges between maize plants
context.note: Makoka Research Station, southern Malawi; randomised block design, 3 replicates, 11.5 x 11.0 m plots, established 1995/96; neutron-probe soil water to 150 cm, 1997/98-1999/00. Comparators: SM = sole maize, no fertiliser or GLM; MP = maize + pigeonpea, no fertiliser or GLM. Authors: rainfall exceeded potential evaporation during the cropping season in all years. Season 1998/99. Comparator MP holds pigeonpea constant so the contrast isolates gliricidia + its GLM. process: WUE = total above-ground biomass of the whole system (trees + crops) / seasonal water use, water use estimated from rainfall + change in 0-150 cm soil water (runoff and drainage assumed negligible). NOT grain yield per water: biomass includes gliricidia. Authors' own caveat (p13-14): soil evaporation and water-table abstraction not quantified; accounting for them might raise sole-crop WUE and lower sole-gliricidia WUE - the contrast is likely overstated. Treatment P value for WUE <0.001 in every season (Table 1).

units.citation: Nguyen et al. (2024). Nature-based solutions for improving food security: A systematic global review. Heliyon.
units.quote:
Three of them were on studies that utilized population 
surveys to find positive results in food access when applied agroforestry in southern Africa, Brazil, and China over extended periods (up 
to 20 years) [34,47,59].

relationship.outcome_raw: food access (FAO food-security dimension: people able to obtain food), agroforestry vs conventional practice, review vote count of population-survey studies

context.practice_as_described: 'applied agroforestry' — the review names the forms as 'alley cropping [34,47,60] and mangrove forest integration [46,62]' (p9); the three cited studies are fertilizer-tree options in southern Africa [34], integrated crop-livestock-forestry systems in the Brazilian Cerrado [47] and rural land-use management for drought adaptation in arid northern China [59]
context.note: process: selection-on-outcome — the review INCLUDED only studies 'in which there was evidence of improvements in at least one food security dimension' (p3), so a positive vote count here is guaranteed by the inclusion rule and says nothing about the share of studies that found no benefit. Three cited primaries: Akinnifesi et al. 2008 [34] (fertilizer trees, southern Africa), Costa et al. 2018 [47] (ICLF, Brazil — an LCA, not a population survey), Lei et al. 2016 [59] (land-use management, arid N China — not clearly agroforestry). Family left agroforestry__cross_family because the three span tree intercropping, agrosilvopasture and an unclear practice; countries span low to upper-middle income so country/income_group left blank. Study periods 'up to 20 years' per the review. PICOS doubt on [59]; prefer the primaries (catalogue #25).
